contests.title: Bloomer School District — School building and improvement bonds

provenance.quote:
INITIAL RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING 
GENERAL OBLIGATION BONDS IN AN 
AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $77,000,000

BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the School District of Bloomer, Chippewa and Dunn Counties, Wisconsin that there shall be issued pursuant to Chapter 67 of the Wisconsin Statutes, general obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $77,000,000 for the public purpose of paying the cost of a school building and facility improvement project consisting of: construction of a new high school with a community performing arts center; safety and security, capital maintenance and building infrastructure improvements at the Middle and Elementary Schools; and district-wide site improvements and acquisition of furnishings, fixtures and equipment.

Adopted and recorded July 15, 2026.

contests.title: Dodgeville School District — Temporary school-revenue increase

provenance.quote:
BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the Dodgeville
School District, Iowa County, Wisconsin that the revenues
included in the School District budget be authorized to exceed the
revenue limit specified in Section 121.91, Wisconsin Statutes, by
$1,900,000 per year for three years, beginning with the 2026-2027
school year and ending with the 2028-2029 school year, for non-
recurring purposes consisting of operational expenses, including
educational programming.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the district to borrow up to $77 million through general obligation bonds to build a new high school with a community performing arts center. It also funds safety, security, maintenance and infrastructure work at the middle and elementary schools, plus school-site improvements, furnishings, fixtures and equipment across the district.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing up to $77 million for these projects.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the district to raise $1.9 million a year above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for three school years, from 2026–27 through 2028–29, for operations, including educational programs. This temporary authorization ends after those years.
